analysis: The code snippet contains three calls to String.substring(int). The first call is 'line.substring("Exception ".length())' inside a block where line.startsWith("Exception") is true. However, startsWith("Exception") does not guarantee that the line has a trailing space; if line is exactly "Exception" (length 9), then beginIndex=10 > length=9, causing IndexOutOfBoundsException. Similarly, the second and third calls are inside checks for materialName.startsWith("MaterialDef") and materialName.startsWith("Material"). The substring constants include a trailing space ("MaterialDef " length 11, "Material " length 9). If materialName is exactly "MaterialDef" (length 10) or "Material" (length 8), the beginIndex exceeds the length. The startsWith checks do not verify the presence of a space, so the condition for IndexOutOfBoundsException is not fully avoided.
answer: The only declared exception for substring(int) is IndexOutOfBoundsException. In the first call, the condition is not fully avoided because the startsWith check does not ensure the line length is at least the length of "Exception ". In the second and third calls, the condition is also not fully avoided because the startsWith checks do not ensure the string length is at least the length of the substring constant with space. Therefore, IndexOutOfBoundsException is not avoided in any of the three calls.
remark: The IndexOutOfBoundsException can be triggered in three scenarios: 1) In the first call (line.substring("Exception ".length())), if the line is exactly "Exception" (9 characters) without a trailing space, the beginIndex 10 is larger than the string length, causing an exception. 2) In the second call (materialName.substring("MaterialDef ".length())), if materialName is exactly "MaterialDef" (10 characters), beginIndex 11 is too large. 3) In the third call (materialName.substring("Material ".length())), if materialName is exactly "Material" (8 characters), beginIndex 9 is too large. These situations occur when the input line or materialName is the exact prefix string without the expected trailing space, which the startsWith checks do not prevent.
